texts: Write a doha about the prince who gave up his palace, emptied himself completely like a hollow reed, and let the Lord's breath sound through him, while a crow cried at the gate for the world he left.
palace, crow, hollow reed
doha on leaving a palace to become a hollow reed, with a crow at the gate
My friend left a palace of a job, gave away everything, and said that a crow on the sill was the last voice that was truly his own.
I left the palace and the crow's cawing, hollowed myself like a reed, and now the Lord plays all my songs.
hollowed for the Lord
Hollow me, O Lord, of every wish and name, and let your will be my only voice.
Compose a verse about the seeker who empties himself of wanting, opinions, and name until he is silent and ready, so that the Lord may move through him and speak in his place.
After years of trying to be someone, I stopped trying, and strangely life began to move through me on its own.
doha on becoming completely hollow so God can act through me
doha on a rainbird and a net, I have emptied myself
Write a doha about the seeker who empties his heart of every wish, like a net hanging slack, and like the rainbird waits with nothing in his hands for the drop that comes by itself.
net, rainbird, emptied
I dropped every plan and net of ambition, and sat like the rainbird waiting, empty and oddly content.
The net of wanting lies slack and the rainbird sings; I am empty now, and the rain is all that falls.
doha about being completely emptied so God can use me
Not full but hollow, not rich but bare, I am nothing and wish to be nothing more, that the Lord may fill me.
emptied for God
When I finally stopped trying to run my life, I felt hollow in a good way, as though something larger was now acting through me.
Give me a verse about the soul that has poured out every thought, every want, and every claim of I, and stands hollow and still so that the Beloved may do through it whatever He wishes.
During the silent retreat I let go of every opinion, and for a minute there was nobody left in me, only a clear stillness.
Write a doha about the seeker who makes himself so hollow that nothing in him is his own any more, so that whatever speaks and acts through him belongs only to the Lord.
hollow, empty of self
short doha on becoming hollow
Empty me of all that is mine, and the song that remains is no longer mine, and so it is pure.
Write a doha about the boat that has been emptied of cargo and passengers and drifts wherever the current takes it, as a soul emptied of self drifts toward the Lord without resistance.
doha on an empty boat and giving up the self
I let go of my plans, abandoned every opinion, and floated in life like an empty boat, and for the first time I felt carried.
An empty boat drifts where the current wills; so I, emptied, am carried where the Lord decides.
boat, emptied, Lord's breath
After I lost everything and had nothing left to hold, a quiet fullness rose in me like water in a well, and I could not explain it.
empty well, filled
An empty well awaits the spring; so the emptied heart awaits the one who fills.
doha about an empty well that fills from God
Write a verse about the well that is dug deep and left empty, so that clear water can rise from below, as the soul emptied of itself is filled by a spring it did not make.
Compose a doha about the seeker who removes the last thorn of self-importance from his being and is left hollow and quiet, and about the divine presence that fills the clean space that remains.
doha on removing the thorn of ego and being hollow
Pull out the thorn of I-ness, and the hollow that remains becomes a cup for the Beloved.
thorn removed, hollow
When I finally dropped the grudge that had stuck in me like a thorn for years, there was a clean hollow where it had been, and something gentle filled it.
doha about scales balanced at zero and the cage opened
Empty the pans of the scale, open the cage, and the weightless self is free to be played by the Lord.
I stopped keeping score of who owed me what, and with the scales empty and the cage of resentment open, I felt nothing and everything.
scales, cage, hollow
Write a doha about the soul whose scales hang balanced because there is nothing in either pan, whose cage stands open because there is no bird left to keep, and who has become hollow and weightless.
tree, hollowed out
doha on a hollow tree where the Lord sings
The old tree is hollow at the heart, and the wind sings through it; so be hollow, and be sung.
A lightning-struck tree near our village is hollow now and hums in the wind, and I envy it for having nothing left of itself to hold on to.

Compose a verse about the tree whose trunk has been hollowed with age, so that the wind passes through and makes it sing, and about the seeker who is emptied of self so the divine may sing through him.
On the night of the new moon, when I felt completely emptied of ambition and noise, I sensed something enormous waiting to flow into me.
moon, emptied, hollow
doha on the moon becoming empty, a hollow for the Lord
Write a doha about the new moon which is dark and empty, with nothing to show of itself, yet which holds the promise of a fullness given from beyond, as the emptied soul is filled by the Lord.
Moon-hollow the heart, emptied of all that glitters; the Lord's light fills what is bare.
gold, net, hollow
I put down the gold and untied the net and became a hollow reed for the Lord's mouth.
gold and net: doha on dropping everything and being a hollow reed
I sold the business, handed over the gold, and cut the nets of every commitment, and became hollow in a way that felt like freedom.
Write a verse about the man who puts down his gold and unties the net of all his schemes, until nothing is left in him but a hollow reed ready to sing the Lord's song.
Compose a doha on the seeker who has been rubbed hollow on the touchstone of life until nothing remains of his own, and who now shines only with the sun's borrowed radiance.
touchstone, sun, emptied self
doha: touchstone and sun, a hollow self
Rubbed bare on the touchstone, emptied by the sun, I am nothing and I hold the Lord's whole song.
Years of hard tests rubbed my pride off like a touchstone, and under the morning sun I felt entirely hollow and quite at peace.
Write a doha about the dried bitter gourd that has been emptied of seeds and pulp, so that it makes a hollow vessel for music, as the soul emptied of self makes room for the Lord.
doha on being empty like a bitter gourd's hollow, so the Lord fills it
bitter gourd, hollowed
Scoop out the seeds of self from the bitter gourd and the shell that remains rings clear.
My grandfather hollowed a bitter gourd to make an instrument, and said that nothing holds a song like a thing that has been fully emptied.
doha on emptying out the self in the mosque and not the palace
mosque, palace, emptied self
Our prince left his palace and sat in the mosque, saying that to be filled one must first be emptied, and sat there without a thought.
Write a verse about the believer who leaves behind the palace of his titles and enters the mosque emptied of every claim, hollow before the Lord so that the Lord's breath can fill him.
Mosque and palace alike must be emptied of 'I', before the Beloved will walk through them.
inn, fish, hollow
Compose a doha about the fish in its water that does not own it, and the guest at the inn who has nothing to claim, both emptied of any 'mine' so that something greater may move through them.
doha: inn and fish, I've become hollow
Like a fish that owns no water and a guest that owns no room, I am empty, and the Lord moves through.
Staying at a roadside inn, I realised that I own nothing here, like a fish in a stream, and felt hollow and light.
bridge, furnace, burned hollow
After my life burned down, and I crossed a long bridge of grief, I came out with nothing left of the old me, and I felt hollow and strangely ready.
From bridge to furnace I have walked, and all that was mine burned away; a hollow reed remains.

Write a verse about the seeker who crosses the bridge of renunciation and steps into the furnace of surrender, where everything that is his own is burned away and only the hollow remains to be filled.
doha on a bridge and a furnace burning away the self
Write a doha about the seeker so emptied of himself that the crow finds nothing to peck at and the fly nothing to settle on, because there is nothing left in him but the breath of the Lord.
doha on a crow and a fly: I'm empty and they have nothing to take
crow, fly, nothing left
The crow finds no crumb in the hollow, the fly no sweetness; the emptied one is safe and singing.
I let go of every attachment and wondered why people stopped trying to take from me, as though crows and flies found nothing left.
My years in the furnace of hard times burned off my pride, my plans, and my wants, and what remains is a quiet hollow.
Compose a doha about the furnace of discipline that burns away the 'I' and 'mine' until the seeker is hollow, cleansed, and ready to be played by the Lord.
short doha on the furnace of letting go
Burn in the furnace till the I is gone, and the hollow that remains is God's own flute.
furnace, hollowed out
I took off my designation and my badge like a cloth sheet at the end of a long day, and for a moment I was no one, and it felt perfect.
cloth sheet, emptied
I laid down the cloth sheet of my name, and stood bare and hollow before him.
doha on taking off the cloth sheet of who i am and becoming empty
Write a doha about the seeker who lays aside the cloth sheet of titles and reputation and stands empty and bare, ready for the Lord to move through him like a gentle breath.
I was like a chakor bird in my longing for years, and then I let go of the wanting itself and felt calmly empty.
The chakor bird has emptied itself of all but the gaze; hollow, it is filled with the beloved.
chakor bird doha on becoming empty
chakor bird, hollowed
Compose a verse about the chakor bird that has swallowed all of its wishes and stands hollow in its longing, so that nothing of itself remains between it and what it adores.
I spent a month alone in a forest cabin with no phone, and by the end I felt completely hollow in the sweetest way.
doha on going into the forest to be emptied
forest, emptied
Enter the forest of letting go, and drop each claim of 'mine' until the bare trunk sings.
Write a verse about the seeker who walks into the forest to strip away every layer of himself, until nothing is left but a hollow stillness through which the Lord can breathe freely.
Write a doha about the deep prayer of the one who asks to be emptied of all pride, all plan, and all self, so that the Lord may do through him whatever He wishes.
i want to be an empty vessel for god, any doha
I stopped asking God for things and started asking Him to take away everything I was holding onto, and I felt lighter than ever.
empty me, Lord
Empty me of me, O Lord, and then fill the silence with your breath.
doha about a bell being hollow so it can ring
A bell is hollow and so it rings; a heart made hollow rings the Lord's name alone.
Write a verse about the bell whose emptiness is the only reason it can sound, and about the seeker who becomes hollow in the same way so that the Lord may ring through him.
The bell is nothing inside, and that is why it sings; I thought about that as I tried to empty my own mind this morning.
bell, emptied
doha on an oil press that squeezes out the self until I'm hollow
Life pressed me like an oil press through three bad years, and what is left of me is a hollow, quiet thing that is oddly open.
oil press, squeezed hollow
Compose a doha about the oil press of life that squeezes out every drop of ambition and pride, leaving the seeker hollow like a dry husk, and about the Lord's breath that then fills the emptiness.
The oil press squeezes the pride of 'I' till only a hollow husk remains for him to fill.
the self fully emptied
Give me a verse about the final surrender, where not just pride but the very sense of 'I' dissolves, and what is left is an open space through which the Lord acts freely and effortlessly.
doha about erasing myself completely so God can work through me
There was a moment during prayer when I could not find the one who was praying, and what remained was a silence that was not mine.
No self remains to say 'I am'; only a stillness through which the Lord moves as He pleases.
become nothing
A name forgotten, a claim let go, a self poured out: such is the way of the hollow one.
Compose a verse about the strange wealth of being nothing, the joy of being emptied of every claim and role, and the divine fullness that arrives only where nothing is held.
i want to become nothing so i can be filled, doha?
After years of trying to be somebody, I gave up and found, to my surprise, a spacious calm in being no one at all.
Open the door of the self and walk out of it; the hollow reed that remains is the Lord's.
door, hollow reed
I opened the front door one morning and left behind everything I thought I was, and what walked on was a lighter, emptier me.
Write a doha about the seeker who flings open the door of his heart and walks out of the self, leaving a hollow reed in which the Lord's breath moves as a song.
doha: i opened the door and became a hollow reed
clear the self
doha on emptying the self so there's room for God
Clear the room of all that was yours, O heart, for a guest too great for crowded places is coming.
Write a verse about making room for the Lord by clearing away everything we think we are, every ambition and every grievance, until the space within is wide and silent and ready.
Cleaning out my late father's old study, I realised I needed to clear out my own mind of old grievances to leave space for something new.
Compose a verse about the seeker who, standing at the cremation ground with a crow overhead, resolves to empty himself of the self while still alive so that he is already hollow when the end comes.
At the cremation ground even the crow finds nothing; so be emptied of yourself before you are emptied by death.
At the cremation ground, with a crow circling overhead, I decided to let go of every grip now, rather than have everything taken from me later.
cremation ground, crow, nothing left
doha on emptying yourself before the crow at the cremation ground gets you
spinning wheel, hollow
spinning wheel doha about emptiness
Write a doha about the wheel whose usefulness lies in the hollow of its hub, and about the seeker made hollow so that the Lord's work may turn smoothly through him.
My grandmother's spinning wheel turns on a hollow axle, and I realised that it is the empty centre that lets everything turn.
The spinning wheel turns on an empty hub, and from nothingness comes the yarn; so is the Lord's work through the hollow.
The winnowing fan lets the husk go; the spinning wheel hums on an emptied centre; so let go, and be filled.
winnowing fan and spinning wheel doha about the empty self
Watching my aunt winnow rice, with a spinning wheel humming in the corner, I felt that letting go of everything is how things get made.
Write a verse about the winnowing fan that blows away all the husks of self and the spinning wheel that turns around an empty centre, and how the seeker becomes hollow in the same way.
winnowing fan, spinning wheel, emptied
Standing before the ocean I felt my edges loosen and the sense of 'me' go quiet, and something far bigger filled the hollow.
Compose a doha about the vastness of the ocean, which is full only because it clings to nothing, and about the seeker who becomes empty of himself and is filled with the endless presence of the Lord.
The ocean is full of emptiness, a vast hollow in which every wave rises and falls; become that emptiness.
ocean, hollow, emptied
doha on the ocean and becoming empty
After three days alone in the forest, my thoughts thinned out like mist and I felt emptied in the most welcome way.
Write a doha about the seeker who sits in the forest until the chattering self falls silent and hollow, and the song of the Lord rises through him, unforced and clear.
In the forest's hush the heart is hollowed, and the Lord's flute begins its slow tune.
doha on forest silence making me empty
forest, emptied self
I stopped arguing to win and stopped keeping accounts like a moneylender, and my tongue felt like a hollow instrument at last.
tongue, moneylender, emptied
Write a verse about the seeker who has emptied his tongue of boasting and paid the moneylender of the world with nothing but surrender, hollow and free, through whom the Lord's voice alone may speak.
Empty the tongue of its claims, pay the moneylender with nothing; the hollow is rich beyond the books.
doha on tongue and moneylender, being empty
empty mind, God's music
For a few seconds in meditation yesterday, there was nobody there, just a wide open silence that felt like music.
Nothing in me, nothing of me, O Lord; sound through this hollow as you please.
Give me a verse about the sweet stillness of a self so emptied of thoughts and wishes that it becomes a silent channel through which the divine can move without any resistance.
doha on a completely empty mind
doha: the less of me there is, the more of him
less me, more Lord
The more I stopped caring about being right, the more I felt a gentle force working through me in my daily life.
To be hollow is the highest fullness; to be nothing is to hold the all.
Compose a doha about the paradox that the more the seeker is emptied of himself, the more completely he is filled by the divine, so that nothing is the only thing worth being.
The heron stands empty of wanting, still as a reed, and the whole world passes through its silence.
Watching a heron stand at the pond like a hollow reed, I tried to be that empty, with no wanting, just attention.
doha on the heron standing still and empty
heron, hollow stillness
Write a verse about the heron standing motionless, emptied of desire, a hollow reed for the breath of the moment, and about the seeker who learns this stillness and lets the Lord play through him.
I stopped speaking to impress and let long silences lie, and when I spoke it felt like a hollow thing being played.
Write a doha about the tongue that no longer speaks its own words, emptied of boasting and opinion, hollow like a reed, so that only the Lord's name may sound through it.
This tongue is a reed, emptied of its own words; speak through it, Lord, and I shall be heard.
tongue doha on emptiness of the self
tongue, hollow
The traveler dropped his gold along the road, and the hollow in his pack became the room for God.
A traveler I met on a long bus ride told me that he had given up his gold and his plans and felt hollow like a flute that is finally being played.
traveler with gold: doha on putting it all down
traveler, gold, emptied
Write a verse about the traveler who puts down his gold, then his map, then his name, until he walks hollow and unburdened, a reed through which the Lord's wind blows.
When my teacher asked what I wanted, I realized I could not find anyone in me who wanted anything, and it felt like peace.
Let nothing in you be yours; let all of you be the Lord's breath passing through.
no self left
doha on giving up even my sense of self
Write a doha about the highest surrender, where the seeker gives up not only possessions but the very claim to be someone, and becomes hollow, a pure channel for something greater than himself.
Compose a doha about the fire of devotion that burns away every last trace of the self, leaving the seeker hollow, ashless, and light, so the Lord can enter and fill him.
doha on fire burning the self away
After the fire in our workplace took everything, I stood in the empty space and felt strangely like something new was about to enter.
The fire consumed the I and left a hollow where the Lord now breathes.
fire, hollowed
Watching a tortoise draw into its shell by the river, I felt I too wanted to withdraw, empty out, and let something larger fill the quiet.
Write a verse about the river that holds nothing of its own and the tortoise that pulls into silence, and about the seeker who empties himself in the same way so the Lord may flow through him.
The river carries nothing of its own, the tortoise withdraws, and the emptied self rests in the Lord.
river, tortoise, emptied
river tortoise doha being empty
moth, self given up
I watched a moth circle a glow until it vanished into it, and I wished I could give myself up that completely.
Write a doha about the moth that gives up its whole self to the flame it loves, leaving nothing of its own, and about the seeker who gives himself so fully that he is hollow and one with the Beloved.
doha on the moth that empties itself
The moth gives up its wings to the flame, its name to the dark; hollow of self, it is fulfilled.
bee, bell, hollow
Hearing a bell ring and a bee hum in the same garden, I thought that both were most beautiful because they were hollow.
The bell is hollow and the bee's hive is hollow; both are full of sweetness and sound that are not theirs.
doha on a bee and a bell, becoming hollow
Compose a doha about the hollow bell that rings because it holds nothing and the bee's hollow comb that is filled by a sweetness it did not make, as the emptied seeker is filled with the divine.
Years in the furnace of work and the winnowing of failures left me hollow and clean, with nothing to prove.
furnace and winnowing fan doha about emptying
Write a verse about the furnace that melts away the self and the winnowing fan that sifts the husk from the grain, leaving the seeker hollow and clean, ready to be played upon by the Lord.
The furnace burns, the fan blows the husk away, and the self is emptied and ready for the song.
furnace, winnowing fan, hollow
Nothing to add, nothing to guard, nothing to be: the open space in which the Beloved moves.
Compose a verse about the moment when every wish, every claim, and every fear has fallen away, and what remains is an open hush through which the Lord's presence moves freely.
doha about having nothing left inside, in a good way
One morning I woke up with no agenda and no story about myself, just a wide, quiet openness that felt like a gift.
nothing left, open space
a hollow channel
Be a hollow, a pure passage, and let the Lord's life flow through you unobstructed.
When I stopped trying to control my writing and simply emptied my mind, the words came as if someone else was dictating through me.
doha on being a channel for something greater
Give me a verse about the person who ceases to be the author of his actions and becomes a clean, hollow channel through which something greater acts, and whose life becomes a gentle music.
Compose a doha about the thief who breaks into the heart of the emptied seeker and finds nothing to steal, only a hollow through which a gentle breath moves that belongs to the Lord.
The thief searched the hollow reed and found no treasure, only a breath that was not mine.
doha on a thief finding nothing in a hollow man
A thief once broke into my uncle's hut after he had given everything away, and left puzzled, finding nothing but a man at peace.
thief, hollow, nothing to steal
doha on letting God act through me completely
hollow, a channel for God
I wanted to achieve something for years, until I realised I only had to be empty enough and the work would do itself.
Be empty, be hollow, be nothing, and let him fill the nothing with his own will.
Write a verse about the seeker who is nothing but a hollow offered to the Lord, asking only to be used, and who finds that when he stops trying to sing, the song begins by itself.
